subject: Re: Encord migration - project thread
text:
Hi Nick,

It was a pleasure meeting you yesterday, and I appreciate your ongoing
support.

Following up on our discussion, I’d like to confirm that the hotkeys are
good to go into production. Additionally, I’d like to request a
customization for the "Pan" feature. Currently, panning requires holding *Shift
+ Left Click*, whereas in edit mode, currently, we use only the left button
to pan images. Allowing panning with just the left button will
significantly improve efficiency, as annotators and reviewers frequently
pan while performing QC. This adjustment would ease the burden of
repeatedly pressing *Shift*.

Please find below:

   - A list of suggestions based on our review of the training material.
   - A list of essential workflow features that need to be incorporated for
   a smooth transition, as some key elements are currently missing. We will
   further be updating as we discover on the go as well.

Encord Training Videos Feedback - Features
<https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1TauOaUp5ngOuJZdq19lJFIF9IQi5asEfMYmA-pE5VI0/edit?gid=0#gid=0>

We are also compiling a list of emails and selected members for the first
training batch, which we will share once finalized.

Additionally, please let us know once the defect labeling datasets have
been uploaded.

Happy to jump on a call if you'd like to discuss these requests in more
detail and their significance to our current workflows.

Best,

Haider

I hope you are doing well. I wanted to follow up on our updated document.

key difference from regular video labeling projects is that, in addition to
the seven preset labels for human activities, we also require a detailed
description of human motion. We believe the level of detail has been
effectively conveyed through these 10 illustrations. A clear and faithful
description of the motion will greatly benefit our project.

subject: RE: Redlines for Encord MSA
text:
Alastair, Nick,

Thanks for bearing with me. Here are the points that ought to keep us busy for our call.

 *   5.1.1 and 5.1.2 – these restrict Invisible’s ability to make use the platform as intended. This point should be led by the business, more so than legal. Invisible retains agents to run tasks for the benefit of its own clients. These paragraphs run counter to the core use case for Encord’s platform.
 *   5.1.10 – Invisible doesn’t agree to this kind of far-reaching commitment. We agree with 5.1.9 and other contract-led restrictions. But a wide claim on “acting contrary to Encord IP” is future-facing and ambiguous.
 *   7.7 – Security Standard – It’d be great to complete this section with commitment to ISO-27001 or a SOC-II Type 2 to further illustrate how 7.7 is interpreted.
 *   8 – IP – Encord struck the IP clause to INV’s benefit. You’ll understand that we require confirmation of ownership of Deliverables (as defined).
 *   10.6 – Invisible does not provide indemnification to its vendors. So long as we agree to read 10.6 as not including an obligation to defend, it can remain. Let’s make sure we align on what’s expected.
 *   Liability – more balance is required (i.e. 11.1 should be mutual). Further, we cannot agree to any uncapped obligations, nor indirect damages. We’d prefer to negotiate a mutual supercap for certain claims, and agree to have Encord be bound by those for some core risks as well (i.e. as a trade-off for removing uncapped liability, we’d agree to have data breaches by Encord capped at the supercap).

Looking forward to meeting and discussing this later today,

Paul
